name: Nicaraguan Seed-Finch
rangeDescription: Caribbean lowlands of nicaragua, costa rica, and western panama
description: What this bird lacks in color, it makes up for with a ridiculously oversized bill. Male is all glossy black, female warm brown.

name: Rondonia Bushbird
rangeDescription: South-central amazonian brazil, in rondônia, southern amazonas, and northern mato grosso
description: Large antbird with a very distinctive, robust upturned bill. Males are all black and females are chestnut with a black throat patch.

name: Mouse-brown Sunbird
rangeDescription: Southern senegal to cameroon, gabon, northern angola, and southwestern democratic republic of the congo
description: A sunbird that is closely tied to water, most often encountered in mangroves, farmlands, and along large rivers as far inland as Mali. Gray-brown above and dingy gray-white below with distinctive bright white spectacles and a relatively large, short bill without much of a curve.

name: Christmas Island Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Christmas island (indian ocean south of java)
description: Generic-looking “white-bellied swiftlet”, but fortunately the only regular one on Christmas Island; migratory House and Pacific Swifts are larger, with bright white rump patches. Note the pale belly, dusky throat, weakly forked tail, and glossy dark upperparts, all traits typical of the genus Collocalia.

name: Mottled Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Makira island (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A tiny round bird with a slightly downturned bill. Brown on the back, wings, and crown.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Crinkle-collared Manucode
rangeDescription: Hills and lower montane forest of new guinea, including misool (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A large bird of foothill and lower montane forest and scrub. All black with red eye, fairly long bill and tail.

name: Trilling Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of northwestern peru to east-central bolivia (santa cruz)
description: Tiny, compact gray bird. Females are slightly duller, with brown lower sides and rump.

name: Sulphur-bellied Whistler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sulawesi
description: A fairly nondescript thick-billed, sparrow-sized songbird. Upperparts are uniform rich brown and underparts whitish, but particularly note the yellow wash to the lower belly and the base of the undertail.

name: Black-faced Hawk
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to southern venezuela, northeastern ecuador, and northern amazonian brazil
description: Smallish chunky hawk. Identifiable by size, shape, and prominent black mask contrasting with orange cere.

name: Blue Ground Dove
rangeDescription: Southeastern mexico (san luis potosí) to northern argentina and southern brazil
description: Attractive small dove of humid forest edges and clearings in tropical lowlands; in some places wanders into small rural villages. Typically rather wary, and most often seen in fast, rather direct flight, as singles or pairs.

name: Grandala
rangeDescription: Alpine meadows of kashmir to southeastern tibet, myanmar, and western china
description: Often seen swirling in flocks above mountain passes, scrubby alpine forests, and highland meadows, this large thrush is unlike any other. Adult male is a deep, almost eye-searing blue with jet-black wings.

name: Marabou Stork
rangeDescription: West-central sub-saharan africa
description: This huge, macabre-looking stork has a massive dagger-like bill and naked pink head and neck that appear severely sunburned. A white ruff and loose inflatable skin on the neck add to its odd appearance.

name: Rufous-tailed Plantcutter
rangeDescription: Central and southern chile and argentina
description: Distinctive bird found in varied wooded and semiopen habitats, from town gardens to meadows and bogs in Andean foothills. Often seen perched on roadside wires.

name: Least Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds canada and usa; winters northern mexico to panama
description: Small, grayish-olive flycatcher; very similar to several other species. Look for relatively bold white eyeing, small bill, and frequent wing flicking.

name: Long-tailed Paradigalla
rangeDescription: Western new guinea (arfak and fakfak mountains)
description: A large, fairly long-tailed bird of montane forest on the Bird’s Head of New Guinea. All black plumage with iridescence on the head, fairly long bill, distinctive, yellow wattle between the eye and the bill.

name: Pycroft's Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds small islands off new zealand coast; ranges to north pacific
description: Small gadfly petrel. Gray upperparts and head, with darker “M” across wings.

name: Black-lored Parrot
rangeDescription: Montane forest of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A big green parrot with a large orange bill, a thin black line between bill and eye, and uniform green wings. Confined to the island of Buru, where it is found in upper levels of forest in foothills and mountains.

name: Black-headed Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Eastern cambodia and highlands of southern vietnam (southern annam)
description: A large, black-capped parrotbill restricted to southern Annam in Vietnam and adjacent areas of Cambodia. Similar in general shape and color scheme to Gray-headed Parrotbill (no range overlap) but with an indistinct dark cheek patch, warmer coloration, and no bold black stripes on the face.

name: Black-breasted Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Tropical and subtropical forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Plump chickenlike bird, stout bill, dark brown overall with blacker breast and face and variable white markings on throat. The blackness of the breast should help separate from other quail.

name: Imeri Warbling-Antbird
rangeDescription: East-central colombia to southern venezuela and far northwestern amazonian brazil
description: Small antbird. Males are streaked black above, with a yellow-tinged throat and rusty flanks.
